For a true 4-channel dash cam covering front, rear, left, and right, my top pick is the Rexing R4 Pro. If you want to capture side-swipes, door dings, and parking-lot incidents, I'd prioritize cameras that actually face the sides of the vehicle rather than cameras designed mainly to record passengers.

My top pick

Rexing R4 Pro

2K front + three 1080p views. Sony STARVIS 2 sensor, GPS, Wi-Fi and parking mode. Best balance of four-direction coverage and front image quality.

Four 1080p directions, GPS, Wi-Fi and infrared night vision. A simpler established choice, but less front-camera detail than the Pro.

Important: Not every 4-channel camera covers the exterior sides

The Vantrue N5S is a well-reviewed four-channel model and was named best four-channel dash cam by Car and Driver. However, its views are front road, rear road, front cabin and rear cabin—not dedicated exterior left/right cameras. 
Car and Driver
+1

If your goal is recording cars hitting your doors or scraping your sides, that distinction matters.

Also, windshield-mounted side cameras record through glass. They may miss close-up impacts below the windows. Dedicated externally mounted side cameras can provide better coverage, but installation is more complicated.

Exterior side coverage — record cars beside me, door dings and side-swipes

chats.answer:
For a true 4-channel dash cam covering front, rear, left, and right, I'd prioritize systems with four independently positioned cameras rather than models advertised as “4-channel” that actually record the front, rear, and two interior views.

The most important features for your setup are:

Dedicated left and right cameras that can capture adjacent vehicles, door dings, and sideswipes.

Good nighttime recording, especially for parking lots.

Buffered parking mode to capture incidents before impact detection.

Reliable continuous recording with minimal overheating.

Readable license plates whenever lighting and camera angles permit.

One important distinction: a side-facing camera mounted inside the cabin may capture traffic beside you, but it won't necessarily capture someone hitting your parked door at close range.

$379.99

One question that changes my recommendation
